QuestifyCoreTests/H5LaunchIssuerTests/te: Intentional replacement of the issuer setup, not byte-equivalent behavior. The old method first required client issuance on the API host, then checked shell host, HTTPS, userinfo and port rejection and a later valid receipt load. Public issue #137 prohibits that issuer setup. The current issuer test requires fail-closed launch; unchanged parent-flow and producer tests independently retain rejection of another host, HTTP, userinfo and mismatched port, with no denied shell load and the appropriate original-receipt boundaries. Low-level load tests retain host/navigation rejection. No server-ticket issuance, domain-isolation deployment or H5 completion flow is claimed.

Intentional contract change, not equivalent coverage. The old method required successful client issuance and a shell on the API host at port 8443. Public issue #137 rejects API-host shell inference and client-issued tickets. The current issuer test explicitly includes that port-8443 API URL and requires no request, launch or shell, with the owned-install receipt still readable. It does not establish a separately hosted server-issued launch or end-to-end H5 completion.

Intentional contract change, not an equivalent rename. Public issue #137 requires a separate registrable H5 hosting domain and server-issued one-use tickets, and identifies client nonce minting plus API-host shell inference as violations. The old method required both removed behaviors. The current issuer test instead requires repeated launch refusal for normal and explicit-port API URLs while preserving exact owned-install receipt reads and zero installation effects. Existing parent/load fixture tests retain nonce-only POST and receipt binding checks. This does not implement or verify a server-ticket or H5 completion flow.
